column1: # THE PURSE -- append-only. FUNDS ARE DERIVED: `python tools/ledger.py`.
# `delta` is a number and `unit` names what it is a number OF. Two columns on
# purpose: 1e has five coin types with real exchange rates, and WHICH COIN is
# sometimes the interesting fact. The day-39 anchor records '28 ep off the orc
# bodies, +14' -- the electrum survives only in that prose, because the
# conversion happened before the column existed. Positive in, negative out;
# 0.1 gp = 1 s.p. tools/ledger.py sums in gp.
# `asset` MUST name a row in campaign/assets.tsv and tools/log.py refuses a row
# without one. That requirement IS the double entry: five errors in this
# campaign were purchases recorded only as a sentence inside the notes column of
# the funds row, with no item row anywhere --
#     the two carts     40 days unrecorded
#     the two mules     ditto
#     the small goods   357 gp, 17 days untracked and never rolled
#     six 50-ft ropes   11 days, while the rope row still said 2
#     dragon scales     carried as unsold long after they were sold
# You cannot write a money row here without naming what the money was for.
# *** WHY THERE IS AN ANCHOR AT DAY 39 ***
# This file was reconstructed on 2026-09-11 from the 4,910-character notes blob
# on the `funds` row of inventory.tsv. FROM DAY 39 ONWARD THE BLOB RECONCILES
# figure the inventory row carries and the figure the tools compute. Every one
# of those movements is a row below.
# BEFORE DAY 39 IT DOES NOT RECONCILE. The day-34 chain (26.1 -> 265.1, less
# 115.5 of outfitting, less 3.2 to Coll, less 18 for Ista's kit) lands about a
# gold piece away from the day-35 opening figure of 150.6, and the blob does not
# say where the difference is. THAT IS THE FINDING, not a failure: a running
# total kept in prose stopped being reconcilable somewhere around day 34 and
# nobody could have known. Inventing eight rows to close a 1 gp gap would put
# false precision into an append-only log, so days 1-38 are one anchor carrying
# the narrative, exactly as the day-39 XP anchor does in encounters.tsv.
# An `anchor` row SETS the purse outright. Everything else adds.

ANCHOR: 595 gp 6 sp. Days 1-38 in one row because the prose blob stops reconciling around day 34 (see header). What it records: 211 gp 6 sp on departure for expedition 6, plus receipts that came in while the party was underground -- ~+312 the day-37 market on the small goods, ~+60 the tool line under Hask, +20 the last iron and salt AT COST, +14 for 28 ep off the orc bodies = 617 gp 6 sp; then LESS 22 gp for Ista's kit on day 39, which this row had never been debited and which the player caught. Earlier landmarks inside the anchor: day 34 receipts +80 iron/salt at cost and +159 the tool line; day-34 outfitting 114 gp 15 sp (10 oil flasks, five daggers, backpack, waterskin, keg and spigot, 18 person-weeks of iron rations); 3 gp 2 sp to Coll for wage arrears; 18 gp Ista's kit; day 35 +61 including Marrow's last ten pair of shears at 26 gp, which Hask UNDERSOLD by nine gold. HASK'S RING-FENCED SEVENTH of the tool line (~36 gp) is NOT in this figure and never has been.
The Draycot licence paid in coin on the table, Ottir witnessing. 25 gp a year for three years, backdated to Michaelmas last. articles.md art. 10

Small-goods receipts for days 38-54 that had never been rolled at the time: 26 (day-44 market) + 21 (day-51 market) + 14 (counter trade). Entered retroactively 2026-09-07, scale anchored by Wend's own day-48 statement that only half had sold, which OVERRIDES the dice
The vial named as REALGAR by Trebb the dyer and sold to the church's limner at Marchford. Valued 45 on 3d6=13; sold 35
The dye to Trebb AT COST, all of it, cash. Reaction 41 -- articles.md's first finding: at cost is a discount and a discount is a gift wearing a trade's clothes

The remaining small goods to OSSERY the mercer, blue shutters, at dusk on market day. HASK SOLD IT and did not undersell, holding his number through two silences. THE LINE CLOSES: 573 gp on 357 gp of cost

Paid at Lyde's door: 25 gp premium plus 6 gp first quarter's board of a year for Meg and Tibb, at 1 gp/month/head (DMG p.28's porter at 1 gp a month WITH quarters). OWING: 18 gp in three further quarterly instalments, next about day 152
Eleven shillings LENT to Dill for his tools -- a LOAN, entered as a debt at his own insistence, repayable out of his first month. He asked for it to be written that way

Toller's FULL valuation for Zelligar's laboratory apparatus, paid the moment he was shown Master Wace's receipt, which recites the contents of Dave's letter. His day-42 condition DISCHARGED after twenty-three days. Over a thousand gold for the first time
Marchford lodging never charged at the time: 8 people, 2 nights, house rule 1 gp/person/night. Booked day 67 when the omission was found
Eight person-weeks of STANDARD rations at 3 gp. Standard, not iron, deliberately -- iron exists to keep a month and a three-day trip does not

SIX 50-ft ropes at 4 s.p. One of the two old ropes was chewed more than halfway through on exp.6 and the plan put eight people on brake lines behind 460 lb. *** THE ROPE ROW STILL SAID 2 FOR ELEVEN DAYS AFTER THIS. This row and the corrected inventory line are the fix ***

First half of 58 gp for the 36-gallon SD cask. Holt named it off the bung without tapping it -- strong stock ale, thirty years and not turned. TWENTY-EIGHT GOLD IS STILL OWING in his own hand against the cask as he draws it, written unasked. That is loop L010, not a receivable in this file

FOUR person-weeks of STANDARD rations at 3 gp, bought the evening before expedition 9. Eight people for seven days is 8 person-weeks; the store held 4.5 (2.5 iron + 2 standard), so this brings it to 8.5 -- seven and a half days for eight. Standing order from the party: EAT THE OLD ONES FIRST, which is right, because standard rations do not keep a month and the day-67 packets are eleven days old while the IRON keeps and is therefore the reserve
TORSAT'S WEEK. Seven nights' bed and board at the house rule of 1 gp/person/night while he serves the DMG p.82 week. Paid up front so nobody has to remember it on day 87

EXPEDITION 10 FOOD. Four person-weeks of standard at 3 gp, bought the morning they turned round. Seven in the field -- Torsat invalid at the Inn, Hask still on the wool road -- so four person-weeks plus the 2.6 already held is about five days for seven, with the 2.5 person-weeks of IRON left untouched as the reserve

TWENTY-NINE COPPER off the two dead kobolds. MM treasure type J individually, 11 and 18. 29 cp = 0.29 gp at 100 cp to the gold -- the smallest sum this campaign has ever logged, and logged anyway because a rule that is skipped when the number is small is not a rule
DELLIE'S WEEK, five nights to day 88 at the house rate of 1 gp/person/night. SHARING TORSAT'S ROOM at her own request -- the rate is per person, not per room

THE WOOL PARTY'S BUY, day 73-83, ten days out. 36 tods at the published 8 gp floor. *** NOT THE PARTY'S MONEY AND DOES NOT MOVE THE PURSE *** -- Wend's venture money. This row exists only to count the party's EXPOSURE against art.7's 500 gp seasonal guarantee. Player's ruling 2026-09-15: track the cap, not the book; Wend's ledger is REPORTED, NOT INSPECTED

FOOD TO COOK, not packed rations -- the player's standing method since the Ludbury road: buy what can be prepared on the way and share the work. Ista taught the camp cooking last time and teaches the rest this time. Two person-weeks' worth of raw food at roughly 4 gp -- cheaper than the 3 gp/person-week of prepared standard rations because it is flour, bacon, onions and a sack of oats rather than packets

THE FORTY JARS SOLD TO TREBB at his own figure of 7 gp, WITHOUT SHOPPING THE TANNER HE HAD JUST NAMED. Dave's standing instruction from the road: he has helped this party repeatedly and for nothing -- named the vial as realgar on day 59 in his own yard with nobody exposed, and named all forty of these today for nothing. The party could have taken Toller's answer and walked it round the corner to a man in a different trade. IT DID NOT

A THIRD LIGHT RIDING HORSE AND TACK, bought at Marchford so somebody can ride to Fenn's while the carts stay put. 25 gp the horse plus 11 gp 5 sp tack -- THE SAME PRICE AND THE SAME PLACE as the light bay bought here on day 59 for Dellie, which is the figure this campaign has already paid and is therefore the figure it pays

WEND MADE WHOLE ON HER 5 GP IN FENN'S BARN -- 5 back plus 1 on top as interest. She put it in on day 27 on the same buy-back terms as the party's 90 and said 'I WANT THE FIBRE, NOT THE FRACTION'; the party changed those terms to coin in her absence and without asking, so it repays her rather than leaving her holding a fraction of something she did not agree to. SHE IS FREE TO GO ON BUYING FROM FENN ON HER OWN ACCOUNT

ACCESS AND COPYING FEE at the Wraye school, 30 gp (2d6=6 x5). The library is A SCHOOL'S, not a church's or a private house's (d6=4), and the terms are ordinary and in coin (d6=1). *** NEOT'S ADVICE IS WHAT BOUGHT THE DOOR: reaction 67 +20 for asking WHAT THE RULES ARE rather than to see anything, and for letting the magic-user do the talking = 87, FRIENDLY. *** They hold identify
COPYING ENLARGE, 25 gp -- desk, supervision, their ink and vellum. NO FEE FOR CHARM PERSON: the check failed at 97 against 75 and there was nothing to copy. One roll bought enlarge AND reduce

THE BRONZE WRESTLERS REALISED at Toller's day-83 valuation of 115, the party having declined his 80 gp cash-now on the 83rd. IT MADE 135 AND HE SAID SO UNPROMPTED -- the 20 is his margin, kept openly, and it is the FOURTH time he has spoken against his own interest. Treasure xp falls due ON REALISATION, not on recovery

FOUR person-weeks of STANDARD rations at 3 gp, the same price paid on days 67, 77 and 80. NINE IN THE FIELD FOR EIGHT DAYS IS 72 PERSON-DAYS; the store held 49 (4.5 standard + 2.5 iron), so 23 short = 3.3 weeks, rounded up to 4. Standard not iron, deliberately, on the day-67 reasoning: iron exists to keep a month and this is not a month

FIFTEEN GOLD PIECES found in the tool racks on the smithy's west wall, section (3,17). *** THE LOCATION WAS FIXED BY TWO ROLLS BEFORE THE PARTY ENTERED THE ROOM -- d6=1 put it in the racks rather than a fire pit or under the anvil, d2=2 put it in the southern of the two west-wall sections -- so it was NOT placed in response to where they chose to look. *** They searched (3,18), the northern west-wall section, an hour earlier and found nothing; the coins were ten feet further along. B1 treasure code B

SEVEN COILS OF 50-FT ROPE at 4 s.p., PHB p.35. ONE for the party, which has been down to two sound coils and a sawn one since six went to Durnhak; SIX for Durnhak, bought against the chance he wants them even though the roll says the six already handed down the shaft discharge the six on his list. 2 gp 4 sp of goodwill with a man who cannot check a price

NINE LARGE SACKS at 16 c.p., PHB p.35 -- one for each of the nine regulars. *** THE PARTY HAS OWNED NO SACK AT ALL FOR NINETY-SIX DAYS *** and is about to carry loose pots and pans down half an hour of unmade outcrop

TWO FLASKS OF LAMP OIL at 1 gp, PHB p.36 -- *** AND TWO IS EVERY FLASK IN WETHERSBY (d6=2, then d2=2). *** Durnhak asked for twelve and has had three; the nine owed him will have to come out of the party's own eight sealed. Oil at the day-100 market on the way back out

EIGHT PERSON-WEEKS OF STANDARD RATIONS -- 56 person-days for TWELVE mouths. *** TWO WEEKS AT THE PHB'S 3 GP AND SIX AT HALF OVER, 4 gp 5 sp, BECAUSE EIGHT IS ALL THE TOWN CAN REACH (d6=4, d6=3) *** -- early spring is the hungry gap before anything is harvested and this is 240 lb of food asked for in one morning off-market. Standard, not iron: standard rations are the COOKABLE kind, which is the camp food the player asked for and it is one line in the price list, not two

TWO HUNDRED IRON SPIKES at 1 c.p., PHB p.35 -- DURNHAK'S, bought out of the 75 owed him. Off MUND THE SMITH, who had the lot in stock. *** THE PARTY ITSELF CARRIES NONE: 9 emplaced in Quasqueton doors, 13 cached under the smithy ash, and the player has chosen to recover those rather than buy more ***

TWENTY POUNDS OF BIG TIMBER NAILS at 5 s.p. the pound -- DURNHAK'S, out of the 75. *** NO 1e CORE BOOK PRICES NAILS; DM call rolled on declared bands (d6=5) against bar iron landing in this district at 2.7 s.p./lb. THE DAY-95 TABLE GUESS WAS ~2 GP AND WAS TOO LOW BY 8 GP OF HIS OWN SHARE *** -- Tristle will tell him on the 101st

EIGHT ELECTRUM off the gnoll's body, corridor north of (13,32), day 99 round 249. MM p.46 individual treasure type L, 2-12 ep, rolled 8. *** VALUED AT 4 GP: rules/equipment.md line 90, 200 cp = 20 sp = 2 ep = 1 gp, and the day-39 anchor set the precedent by recording 28 ep off the orc bodies as +14. *** Tristle searched it; on the party's persons per articles.md, there being no third place for money

FIVE GOLD off the same body. MM p.46 individual treasure type M, 2-8 gp, rolled 5. *** A gnoll carries BOTH L and M and treasure.py said 'no individual treasure' until it was fixed today -- its regex matched only 'L individually' and the MM writes the gnoll as 'Individuals L, M'. Both coin rolls are recorded in the DM notes because treasure.py rolls through random and not dice.py, so they are NOT in rolls.tsv

TWENTY-THREE ELECTRUM off the four orc squatters in the library, day 99 round 320. MM individual treasure type L, 2-12 ep each: 5, 9, 2, 7. *** VALUED AT 11 gp 5 sp on the 2 ep = 1 gp rate (rules/equipment.md line 90), the same rate the day-39 anchor used for 28 ep off the orc bodies and the gnoll's 8 ep used this morning.

TWO NIGHTS' BED AND BOARD -- Dave and Tristle, one night each, at the house rate of 1 gp/person/night (rules/equipment.md, the rate this campaign has used since expedition 4 and the same one Torsat's week and Dellie's week were charged at). *** d6=3: ROOM BUT SHARED -- pallets in the common room on the eve of market day, because the town is filling. Holt found them something; he is not a stranger and the party holds his 28 gp on the cask. *** THE HORSES COST NOTHING: they went to WEND'S BARN, which is where the party's three horses live and which Coll runs. 'Stable them like we normally do' is the barn, not a hired stall.
THREE LARGE METAL-BOUND BOOKS SOLD TO TOLLER at 4 gp each, his own valuation given undressed and unasked. Out of area 12, the library, on day 99.

SEVEN SMALLER VOLUMES SOLD TO TOLLER at 2 gp each. *** HIS REASON FOR THE LOW NUMBER IS THE ONE HE GAVE ON DAY 16 when he argued the party out of a city sale against his own pocket: the market here for ordinary books is thin and histories and treatises are stock that SITS.
THREE SCROLLS out of area 12's east-wall rack, sold to Toller at 5 s.p. each -- squarely his line, unlike the copper wire, which he named a smith's business and sent them to Mund for.

*** THE UP-FRONT SETTLEMENT AT THE WATERCOURSE, CASH AGAINST GOODS IN ONE TRANSACTION, which is what the player asked for on day 99 and what Durnhak agreed. *** 37 gp is the up-front figure TRISTLE HIMSELF NAMED, unprompted, on day 95 -- and the player's reading reconciles it: the iron is estimated at 150 gross, Durnhak's half is 75, and A QUARTER OF THE GROSS IS 37.5. *** THE GOODS COUNT TOWARD IT AND ARE NOT ON TOP OF IT -- 'take it out of the seventy-five' is netting language, and the DM had read it as sequencing and charged a quarter of the REMAINDER, which would have handed Durnhak 43 gp 1 sp of his 75 before a bar was sold. PLAYER-CAUGHT: 'if we give him all these goods, and then a quarter of the remaining profit, he's getting money in advance. Do you think he meant to do that?' HE DID NOT -- he refused the party's offer to settle up front precisely so he would not be paid for iron that might prove worthless. *** SO: 37 promised, LESS 32 gp 4 sp of stores actually delivered (6 coils rope, 11 flasks of the 12 asked, the hooded lantern, 200 spikes, 20 lb nails) = FOUR GOLD SIX SILVER IN COIN. *** REMAINING TO HIM AFTER THE SALE: about 37 gp 5 sp, and the 75 is an estimate he named as one.

*** THE WHOLE CRAG SALVAGE LOT, SOLD TO MUND THE SMITH AT THE DAY-100 MARKET FOR 117 GOLD. *** 421 lb out of areas 13 and 18 plus the kitchen -- seventy feet of heavy chain, thirteen shovels, a smith's entire hand-tool set, a 12-inch iron vise, fifteen chisels, a mason's and a cobbler's toolbox, hand bellows, sixty unfletched arrows, thirteen pots and pans, the sheave block AND THE 150 LB CAST KETTLE. *** 4d10+100 = 117. No 1e book prices any of it and assets.tsv records only weights, so the figure is a DM call on a declared basis: WORKED TOOLS ARE WORTH FAR MORE THAN THEIR IRON. The party's own bar runs ~0.25 gp/lb; a smith's kit is not bar. Anchored against this campaign's own salvage sales -- the SD barrel at 58, the bronze wrestlers at 115. *** HASK SOLD IT AND HASK CANNOT READ OR RECKON. d6=1: HE DID NOT ASK COLL FOR SARN and there is NO ITEMISED RECORD -- he has the money and the buyer's name and nothing else. d6=1: HE DID NOT ASK WEND ABOUT THE KETTLE EITHER, and it went with the lot. *** Both were explicit instructions. This is not theft and not malice: the money is right. THE RECORD SIMPLY DOES NOT EXIST.

column7: the nine -- Dave, Yrtone, Torsat, Tristle, Frython, Blartho, Hask, Dellie, Ista
column9: *** THE 117 SPLIT EVENLY NINE WAYS, THIRTEEN GOLD EACH, AND IT DIVIDES EXACTLY. *** The player's call: 'if he sold and got it done and it's less work all around, great.' Hask's two disobeyed instructions treated as a job done rather than a failure, which is the party's judgement to make and is not obviously wrong -- the money was right and came over whole. *** BRAND IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED and the player said why: 'he signed on for no money.' He asked to be taught the trade, not paid, and the party is holding to the terms HE set. He still draws his half share of EXPERIENCE. *** HOW IT LANDED: HASK 76+30 = 106, ENTHUSIASTIC. Dellie and Ista 52+30 = 82, favourable. *** THE +30 IS ARGUED AND NOT ASSUMED: articles.md's gifts-fail-work-lands table records 'Hask, asked to PICK his share in front of Wend -- 24 -- badly'. That was a man ASKED TO CHOOSE, put on the spot in front of the factor of the hundred. THIS IS AN EVEN SPLIT STATED -- everybody the same, nobody choosing, nobody singled out -- and it is his cut of a job he did. The same figures gave 100 and 109 when Hask was handed a decision and a job. *** ⚠ THE MONEY IS NOW PERSONAL AND NO TOOL HERE TRACKS PERSONAL PURSES. money.tsv computes the PARTY purse only.

column7: the six PCs -- the purse is theirs
column9: *** CORRECTION, PLAYER-CAUGHT: I TOOK ALL 117 OUT OF THE PURSE AND SHOULD HAVE TAKEN 39. *** Player: 'I think you took everyone's share of salvage out of the party purse but you should have only taken Hask, Dellie and Ista's.' *** THE DISTINCTION IS REAL AND I COLLAPSED IT: THE SIX PCs ARE THE PARTY. Dave, Yrtone, Torsat, Tristle, Frython and Blartho pool everything -- the purse IS their money and always has been -- so dividing 13 gp to each of them and then removing it from the purse takes the same coin out twice and leaves it nowhere. HENCHMEN ARE DIFFERENT: Hask, Dellie and Ista are paid out, which is exactly the half-share/full-share line characters.tsv already draws for experience. *** SO: 117 nine ways is 13 each; 6 x 13 = 78 STAYS, 3 x 13 = 39 LEAVES. Net outflow 39, purse 1,124 and not 1,046. *** THIS ROW RESTORES THE 78. Appended, not edited -- money.tsv is append-only and a wrong figure is corrected by a superseding row. *** AND IT IS THE SAME CLASS OF ERROR AS THE SPIKE DOUBLE-COUNT IN L057: treating a thing as leaving when it only changed label.

*** TWENTY-NINE BARS OF IRON SOLD TO MUND THE SMITH, 609 lb, 146 GOLD. *** Priced against the party's OWN REPRICED BOARD, which now shows the road in the price -- a comparable 600 lb reads at its laid-down ~160, not the Ludbury 100 it carried before L024 was fixed. His 146 is a modest discount off his own alternative cost for taking the lot today with no waiting on a Ludbury run. *** HALF OF WHAT THE IRON MAKES IS DURNHAK'S: 73 gp. He has had 37 (32 gp 4 sp in stores, 4 gp 6 sp in coin), so 36 gp falls due to him. *** AND TRISTLE'S ESTIMATE DOWN THE SHAFT ON THE 95th WAS ~75. It came out at 73. Good to a gold and a half, to a man who could not check a figure of it.

TWENTY FEET OF FINE COPPER WIRE, off the area 13 rack, 5 gp. Toller would not have it and named Mund, who wanted it (d6=5) -- fine drawn wire is LABOUR not material and nobody in the north hundred draws it. *** WHOLLY THE PARTY'S AND NOT DURNHAK'S: the bargain covers metal hauled to the area 19 shaft and carted off the crag by his people. The wire was carried out the front door by the party.

*** THE SIX ROPES BOUGHT FOR DURNHAK ARE UNDONE -- THE PURCHASE WAS MADE ON MY BAD ADVICE AND THE PLAYER IS REVERSING IT. *** Player, day 102: 'we bought those 6 ropes b/c that was in your list of things we had to buy for Durnhak - let's just undo that.' *** AND THE MONEY ROW ITSELF SAYS WHY HE IS RIGHT: 'SIX for Durnhak, bought against the chance he wants them EVEN THOUGH THE ROLL SAYS THE SIX ALREADY HANDED DOWN THE SHAFT DISCHARGE THE SIX ON HIS LIST.' The obligation was already met on day 95. My stores account carried six coils as still owing, the party bought six on that basis, and the account was wrong. *** 6 coils at 4 s.p. = 2 gp 4 sp back. THE ONE COIL BOUGHT FOR THE PARTY STANDS -- it was a real need, they were down to two sound and a sawn one. *** Reversed rather than treated as a gift to Durnhak because he never asked for them, never received them, and does not need them.

*** SEVEN DAGGERS SOLD, day 103. Ista keeps the one. *** At HALF THE PHB LIST PRICE, which is this campaign's settled resale rule -- rules/equipment.md: 'No 1e table sets a resale price for used arms; the campaign has settled on half the PHB list price, which is what expedition 1's salvage fetched.' Dagger and scabbard is 2 gp (PHB p.35), so 1 gp each, 7 gp the seven. *** NO SCENE AND NO NPC, at the player's request. A small sale of ordinary ironmongery in a market town does not need a reaction roll. *** THE CLERICS NEVER COULD USE THEM (PHB p.20 forbids edged and pointed weapons) and of the six non-clerics only Ista has ever drawn one -- Frython's was non-proficient at -5 and he never once used it.

TWO SPEARS SOLD at half the PHB list of 1 gp = 5 sp each, day 103, no scene. *** THE THIRD GOES TO HASK, who is SPEAR-PROFICIENT (characters.tsv: short sword, spear, sling) and has used one before -- the player remembered it and the sheet confirms it. *** Dave and Torsat are both spear-proficient too and both carry long sword and short bow; Tristle's spear was the deliberate non-proficient second-rank reach and CHECKLIST 3 says not to 'correct' that -- but with only one spear left it goes to the man who can actually use it.
The two sealed flasks the town has -- the whole of its stock since day 97 (d6=1, then d2=2). PHB p.35, 1 gp the flask.

36 tods sold, 26 gp the tod (best of several offers shopped, day 108). The 288 gp of art.7 capital that bought this lot (day 83, book=art7) returns here, plus 648 gp of profit -- ALL OF IT the party's own: ongoing-venture has no other investor and Wend is paid a wage, not a share (checked against the record, day 103). Closes the cycle the day-83 buy opened against the art.7 exposure cap.
All 55 flasks on offer, 6 s.p. each -- a city bulk price (d6=1, cheaper than the 1 gp PHB baseline). Bought day 108.
day 119: 11 sp off the dead berserker (MM treasure type K individually, rolled: 11 sp), found by Tristle's search
